reference: icon-engineC2-597699-masked.png (geometry-matched, isolates material). Every round also cross-scored against icon-engineC-c57a8c-masked.png (C1, the material winner) - the two agree, which is what makes the replay finding real.
metric_tier: r00-r07: numpy (luminance+ssim+edges, NO LPIPS) - a degraded instrument. r08-torch onward: full (lpips), via /tmp/fidelity-venv/bin/python. All of r00-r07 were re-scored at full tier; see full_tier_replay.

rounds.change: the first material rebuild, scored as it stood
rounds.note: Reference is icon-engineC2-597699-masked.png: C1 won the material read, C2 was taken as the reference because it shares this composition, so the residual isolates material instead of arguing about geometry.

Depth-binned both rasters and the master: core read L 0.428 S 0.795 against C2's 0.466/0.783 and C1's 0.469/0.751. Lifted the gel ramp. Composite moved -0.0008, which is the point - the score is a proxy, the material was wrong.

rounds.change: rolled arrises: page slab crest, flap cut-face crest
rounds.note: Perpendicular profiles: my page edge blew out to L 0.996 where the reference crests only +0.03 over its face, and my flap's free edge had no crest where the reference carries one at 0.839. Both fixed and the crest landed at exactly 0.839 - but the wide falloff behind it filled the flap/page value gap and dropped 32px self_contrast 0.365 -> 0.339.

rounds.change: the same crest with the falloff bounded
rounds.note: Narrowed the falloff. Self_contrast unchanged at 0.339, so the falloff was not the cause: the crest itself sits on a live figure-ground boundary.

Only the cut faces whose outward normal turns into the key get the crest; the ones facing away get a slight darkening instead. Physically right, halves the crest's extent, and the boundary that carries the 32px silhouette stays hard. Self_contrast recovered to 0.3546 and the floor stopped firing; the gate still rejected on a 0.0056 drop in the 16px similarity term. Kept - the 16px squint renders identically.

The darkest pixel under the reference's page reads 0.647; mine reached only 0.804, so the sheet was floating rather than resting. Three radii instead of two. Best 32px (0.6542) and 128px (0.4894) composites of the whole run; rejected on 256px alone.

rounds.change: the dark end of the gel ramp, as its own statistic
rounds.note: r01 fixed the core and left the darkest accent at 0.388 where the references read 0.337 and 0.212 - a ramp with the right middle can still have no bottom. Adding a deep band changed nothing, which was the finding: see r07.

rounds.change: the AO clip bug, and the ramp rebalanced
rounds.note: Both occlusion bands had been offset to the wrong side of the crease and clipped away by flapClip for the whole run, which is why the darkest pixel would not move however hard the opacity was pushed. Fixed, then the gel ramp was rebalanced against the core and the darkest pixel together. Gate rejected it at -0.0284 because C2's flap is FLAT and this one now has a real shadow where the V closes. Matching the reference's flatness would cost the fold its volume, which is the icon's whole argument. Rubric outranks gate.

rounds.change: no edit; r07 re-scored at full tier
rounds.note: The honest baseline. 1024 composite 0.5130 against the 0.5417 numpy claimed, LPIPS 0.4883. LPIPS engages only at 256 and 1024, which is exactly where material is judged.

rounds.change: gel ramp reverted to r04 values (#CE3A16/#E85128/#F46F41)
rounds.note: r07 had lightened the ramp. Reverting moved 1024 LPIPS by 0.0000 and recovered +0.030 of absolute self-contrast at 1024 (0.4447 -> 0.4748) and +0.017 at 32px. The finding is the null: a hue/value ramp shift is nearly invisible to a deep-feature metric, so the ramp was not the perceptual regression. Kept anyway - self_contrast is reference-free and it is the legibility number.

rounds.change: r05 contact-shadow round reverted to two bands; crease AO probed absent, then kept
rounds.gate: ACCEPT vs r08 baseline (+0.0043); REJECT vs r09 on 32px composite alone
rounds.note: This was the regression: reverting r05's third shadow band and raised opacities moved 1024 LPIPS -0.0148 of the 0.0181 total gap. Then, per the loop's r03 lesson, the crease AO was scored ABSENT before being repaired: deleting it entirely bought a further -0.0035 LPIPS and was DECLINED. C2's flap is flat, so converging on it costs the fold its volume - the icon's whole argument and its only real separation from armada-sync. Rubric outranks gate. Keeping the AO also gave the run its highest 32px self_contrast (0.3640), so the reference-free metric agreed with the rubric.

Found by the blind panel, not by the metric. On r10 vs r07 both judges that ran preferred r07 and both independently named the same defect: a 'tighter diagonal specular ... more like a gloss streak than volume'. It was a pure white hairline in a scene where nothing emits white light - Tahoe grammar #6 sanctions one soft light and zero hard speculars. Re-panelled on r11 vs r07 with the order reseeded, the judges REVERSED and preferred r11, citing 'less hard-edged specular streak on the orange face'. LPIPS moved +0.0011 (noise) while the composite hit its best mean of the whole run, 0.5837 - the panel saw something the metric cannot.

r10_vs_r07.defect_named_by_both: tighter diagonal specular, reads as a gloss decal rather than volume

r11_vs_r07.cited: less hard-edged specular streak; highlight falloff gentler and less pin-sharp

panel.judges: claude (opus) + cursor/grok ran both rounds; openai judge failed both (no OPENAI_API_KEY), recorded not dropped
panel.reading: The composite scored the r10->r11 edit as noise (+0.0011 LPIPS) while the blind panel went from 2-0 against to 2-0 for. Clearest evidence in this commission for panel > gate.

full_tier_replay.what: r00-r07 were re-scored with torch+lpips against both rasters. The run went BACKWARDS and shipped its worst take. Composite 1024 r00 0.5233 -> r07 0.5130; 1024 LPIPS 0.4730 -> 0.4883 (higher is worse). Best-ever on the material metric was r04 (LPIPS 0.4702); the shipped r07 was last of the eight.
full_tier_replay.why_it_was_invisible: The numpy stack has no perceptual term. r05's third contact-shadow band and r07's ramp lightening both read as roughly neutral to luminance+SSIM+edges while LPIPS and absolute self-contrast both fell. The gate also REJECTED r02/r03/r04, which the full tier shows were the run's best rounds.

stopping: Stopped at r11 on the promotion rule: return the best-ever checkpoint, not the latest, and promote on the panel rather than the gate. r11 leads r07 on 1024 composite (+0.0067), on LPIPS against both rasters, on self-contrast at every size, and on the blind panel. Structural ceiling: edge F1 is 0.057 at 1024 because the reference is an inset card on a backdrop and the master is full-bleed - a fifth of the composite was never winnable and should not be chased.
